name: Manosphere
summary: The manosphere is a loose online network of men's rights, pick-up artist, Men Going Their Own Way and incel communities that share a 'red pill' view that men, not women, are the disadvantaged sex and that feminism has feminised society. It holds that gender differences are biological, defends traditional gender roles and the traditional family, and treats feminism and sometimes the welfare state as destroyers of family and society. Its sources say little on economics, foreign affairs or government structure.
scope: The online network the scholarship names the manosphere (Lilly's taxonomy of MRA, MGTOW, PUA and incel communities, as used by Horta Ribeiro et al.) and its own writing, taken as the shared worldview they describe: the red-pill belief that women hold more power than men and that masculinity is under siege. Where the communities diverge (for example on gay rights or marriage) the answer is a split or null. It excludes the offline men's rights movement, which has its own entry, except where Lilly describes positions the whole network holds.

traditional-family.rationale: Lilly finds MRA and PUA writers championing the traditional nuclear, patriarchal family as the best form of family organization and the basis of a strong society, and Return Of Kings tenet 3 credits past traditions with a net benefit to the family unit; MGTOW writers reject marriage for themselves but do not argue against the family as such.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Lilly finds the manosphere united by the belief that women dominate and are more privileged than men; it treats 'the patriarchy' as a feminist myth or says it has already been undone, so it rejects the claim that society systematically advantages men.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The shared worldview in Lilly's reading is that men, not women, are the oppressed sex; the MRA subculture campaigns on men's legal disadvantages and the manosphere casts masculinity as in crisis.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Lilly reports MRAs and father's-rights groups campaigning on the claim that half of domestic violence victims are men and attacking the feminist 'domestic violence industry'; the PUA branch shares the 'hysteria' framing.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Lilly finds MRA and PUA writers alike equating gender with biology and denying it is socially constructed ('masculinity is what men are like'); Return Of Kings tenet 4 makes testosterone the biological cause of masculinity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: The manosphere treats sex differences as biological reality and rejects constructionist accounts of gender (Lilly), which leaves no room for sex itself being constructed.

evolved-behavioural-sex-differences.rationale: Return Of Kings tenet 1 says men and women differ genetically in body and mind and that sex roles evolved in all mammals, humans included; Lilly records evolutionary arguments across the PUA and MRA writing.

equal-conscription.rationale: Lilly lists male-only selective service among the MRA subculture's issues and quotes writers citing military conscription as evidence that men are disadvantaged; the sources do not say whether the fix is to include women or to end the draft, and either satisfies this statement.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Lilly reports manosphere writers arguing that families are stronger and more moral when led by an authoritative father figure, with traditional gender roles; the sources do not frame it as a statement about marital authority in law.

cut-welfare.rationale: Return Of Kings tenet 7 says socialism and feminism aim to impoverish the state through large welfare entitlements, and Lilly quotes writers casting the welfare state as a substitute father paying single mothers; the MRA programme calls for ending aid programmes that serve only women, which is narrower than cutting welfare generally.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The MRA programme Lilly records includes abolishing sex-based affirmative action programmes, which opposes legally required parity of women and men in public bodies.

femininity-compatible-with-feminism.rationale: Lilly finds manosphere writers saying feminism and the sexual revolution masculinise women and destroy femininity, and Return Of Kings says it wants men masculine and women feminine against feminist androgyny.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Lilly finds the sources divided: PUA writers tie gay marriage to the destruction of the family and society, while A Voice for Men posts at times present the men's movement as an ally of gay men.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Return Of Kings tenet 7 says socialism and feminism aim to impoverish the state through large welfare entitlements, and Lilly quotes writers casting the welfare state as a substitute father paying single mothers; the MRA programme calls for ending aid programmes that serve only women, which is narrower than cutting welfare generally. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

notes: Few answers because the sources describe a shared grievance worldview, not programmes. Searched themes: gender and family (covered), welfare, conscription, hate speech, sex work, abortion, marriage law, sexuality, suffrage (a single Return Of Kings writer's call to end women's voting is one voice, not a network position, so null), religion, economy, foreign affairs and government. Divorce and custody reform is a stated MRA concern but no statement here says what the reform is. Colour is a guess. Lilly also records that the network divides on capitalism (most celebrate it, about 6 percent of cases attack it) and on religion, so no economic or secular-religious position is recorded; political support for Trump and links to the alt-right are reported as tendencies, not tenets.
